## Honest analysis — 2026-08-04 baseline

**One-line read:** on a tiny hand-styled page webengine is at fidelity parity and
~10× faster; on a text-heavy page with inline styling it is roughly half-right
and ~2.5× faster; on any page whose look depends on an **external stylesheet**
the fidelity collapses (SSIM 0.23–0.27, ~98% of pixels differ) because the render
pipeline **does not fetch `<link rel=stylesheet>` yet**. The content is parsed and
painted — it is the *styling*, not the text, that is missing.

We are **not yet "as good as Chromium headless."** We are competitive on the
narrow slice we fully support (small, self-contained, inline-styled static pages)
and we are faster there, but the general web is dominated by external CSS and
that is the single biggest gap this baseline exposes.

### Where we are at / above parity

- **`example.com/` — SSIM 0.954, pixdiff 1.5%, 10.3× faster.** This is the honest
  win: a page with a single inline/UA-defaulted style block. webengine reproduces
  the text, background and link colour almost pixel-for-pixel and renders it in
  **284 ms vs Chrome's 2.9 s** (Chrome's number includes process/tab spin-up; even
  so the pure-Go path is dramatically cheaper). The residual 4.6% SSIM gap is
  vertical centring (`margin: … auto` / viewport-height centring) and font
  substitution — Chrome vertically centres the block, webengine top-aligns it (see
  the montage: identical text, different Y).

### Where we are partway

- **Wikipedia (Go article) — SSIM 0.596, pixdiff 15.6%, 2.5× faster.** Wikipedia
  ships a lot of its typographic styling inline / in served `<style>`, and the
  Phase-1 float layer puts the infobox on the right, so a real chunk of the page
  lines up. The 0.40 SSIM deficit is honest: Chrome shows the styled sidebar,
  infobox chrome, link/section colours and reference superscripts that our
  UA-default cascade flattens, and our full page runs 27081 px tall vs Chrome's
  21574 px because unstyled blocks stack taller. 0.596 is "recognisably the same
  article, clearly not the same rendering."

### Where the gap is large (and exactly why)

- **`pkg.go.dev/net/http` — SSIM 0.267, pixdiff 98.8%, 0.45× (2.2× *slower*).**
- **`go.dev/blog/` — SSIM 0.233, pixdiff 98.3%, 0.80×.**
- **`react.dev/` — SSIM 0.249, pixdiff 90.7%, 0.87×.**

  All three fail for the **same root cause, and it is not JavaScript**: the
  cascade (`css.CascadeVW`) already *accepts* external sheets
  (`externalSheets []string`), but `engine.RenderDocument` calls it with **`nil`**
  — nothing fetches the `<link rel=stylesheet>` files. So these pages render with
  only UA defaults + inline `<style>`: a single left-hand column of correctly
  parsed text with no header bar, no dark code blocks, no grid, no theme. The
  montages make it plain — **every word is present** on the webengine side; the
  teal/dark chrome, the two-column layout and the code-block panels are all that's
  missing, and that misalignment alone drives pixdiff to ~98%.

  `react.dev` is the instructive one for the "SPA gap": it is **server-side
  rendered**, so webengine actually shows the hero copy, the code samples and even
  fetches the React logo image. Its low score is **also external-CSS**, not blank
  content. A *purely* client-rendered SPA (empty `<div id=root>` filled by JS)
  would instead show near-nothing until Phase 2 (goja) runs its scripts — this set
  doesn't contain such a page, and the report should not pretend react.dev is one.

  Note the speed inversion on `pkg.go.dev`: **12.4 s** for webengine. Laying out
  an 83134-px unstyled linearisation is expensive; once external CSS constrains
  the box tree (and content is not stacked full-width) both fidelity **and** speed
  should recover.

## Per-phase targets (how the gap closes)

| Phase | Change | Target on the affected pages |
|-------|--------|------------------------------|
| **1.5 — external CSS fetch** | Wire `<link rel=stylesheet>` fetching into `RenderDocument` (fetch + pass to `CascadeVW`; the cascade already supports it). | pkg.go.dev / go.dev / react SSIM **0.25 → 0.55–0.70**, pixdiff **≈98% → <45%**. Biggest single win; also fixes the pkg.go.dev speed regression. |
| **1.6 — layout completeness** | `border-radius`, `box-shadow`, gradients, sticky/absolute/fixed positioning, real font metrics/substitution, vertical `margin:auto`. | example.com **0.95 → 0.98+**; Wikipedia **0.60 → 0.75+**; styled pages **+0.05–0.10** each. |
| **2 — JavaScript (goja)** | Run page scripts so client-rendered DOM is populated and interactive UI (menus, tabs, search) appears. | Client-only SPAs from near-blank → **0.6+**; SSR pages gain the post-hydration bits. |
| **3 — polish to parity** | Sub-pixel AA parity, colour-management (sRGB), web-font loading, scroll/overflow clipping. | Text-heavy static pages **0.90+ SSIM**; hold or extend the speed lead where we already win. |

**Speed stance:** on self-contained static pages we are already faster than
headless Chromium and should stay there; the honest goal is to reach Chromium's
*fidelity* on static content without giving up that speed. The `pkg.go.dev` 12 s
is a red flag to fix in Phase 1.5, not a property to accept.

## Reproduce

```sh
cd bench
CHROME_BIN="/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" \
  go run ./cmd/compare -urls urls.txt
```

Re-run at the end of each phase; the table above is regenerated, this analysis is
preserved. Track SSIM up and pixdiff down per row.
